transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-30 15:00 PST
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Anya Roberts (Redwood CSM); Dr. Maya Singh (CTO, Kepler), Carlos Ruiz (Head of Infrastructure), Lena Park (Security Architect), Omar Ahmed (Product).

Summary:
Quick POC scoping for Private networking and data residency for a 2-week proof-of-concept. Main concerns: VPC peering vs PrivateLink, egress constraints to third-party services, region placement (US-only vs EU), and clear success criteria around latency/p95 and throughput. Discussed workload sizing (concurrent users, tokens per request), benchmark plan, and timelines.

Topics:
- Network topology options (VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink, Transit Gateway)
- Data residency and region requirements (US east vs EU-west)
- Egress filtering and allowed outbound endpoints
- Benchmark plan and success criteria (latency p50/p95, tokens per second, error rate)
- POC timeline and next steps

Action items (auto section): see metadata action_items above.

Transcript body:
00:00 Jordan Lee: Hey everyone thanks for taking the time, do you all see the call notes? um great. quick intro, I'm Jordan, I'm the AE working with Kepler for the POC, Priya and Marco from our SE team will run the bench and the network plan.
00:18 Dr. Maya Singh: Thanks Jordan. We want to make sure this POC validates network isolation and residency. our legal is pretty strict — PHI flow, so we need either private VPC peering into Redwood Private or some equivalent.
00:36 Priya Nair: Totally, thanks Maya. To kick off, can you confirm target regions and whether data must be strictly US-resident or multi-region? that drives the deployment plan and endpoints.
00:51 Carlos Ruiz: Primary target is us-east-1 for now, we might expand to eu-west later but initial production must stay in US only. Also we have strict egress rules — all outbound traffic must go via our proxy and we block unknown external endpoints.
01:10 Marco Diaz: ok that helps. two main options we typically see: VPC peering from your VPC to our Private VPC, or AWS PrivateLink endpoints for the Redwood Private control plane and serving endpoints. each has tradeoffs.
01:28 Lena Park: can you clarify tradeoffs? specifically we are worried about cross-account routing and whether traffic traverses the public internet.
01:36 Marco Diaz: yes, great question. with VPC peering, it is direct L3 routing between VPCs — traffic stays on the AWS network and doesn't go via the public internet, but you need route table entries and peering limits matter for very complex topologies. PrivateLink (NLB + interface endpoints) gives you per-service ENIs in your VPC and is more restrictive — it limits to the service endpoints but simplifies security policies and avoids route table changes. Transit Gateway is also an option at scale.
02:05 Dr. Maya Singh: so PrivateLink sounds safer from our security team's perspective but is there a latency hit compared to peering?
02:13 Priya Nair: Latency difference is usually small but depends on pathing and NLBs. for our benchmarks we'll measure p50/p95 for both short prompts (~20 tokens) and longer sequences (~512 tokens). target for your interactive workflows we typically aim for p95 under 300-400ms for short prompts, but we can tune batch sizes and KV cache to meet your needs.
02:36 Omar Ahmed: our baseline QPS for the pilot will be about 10 concurrent calls, peak 50 QPS with average 150 tokens per request. storage of logs will need to be in our account or encrypted with a KMS we control.
02:53 Jordan Lee: good; to confirm success criteria: 1) network isolation with no public egress for model inference traffic, 2) p95 latency at or below 350ms for short prompts under pilot load, 3) throughput to support 50 QPS with <1% error rate, 4) security checklist (SOC2, audit logs, SAML SSO). Are we aligned?
03:16 Dr. Maya Singh: yes that seems reasonable, but we also need evidence that no data leaves the region — can you support a private control plane in our region?
03:24 Marco Diaz: we can deploy Redwood Private in us-east-1 and pin the serving endpoints to that region. for compliance we can provide audit logs and KMS integration so keys never leave your control if you want.
03:38 Lena Park: about egress: our infra blocks external DNS and only allows specific FQDNs. can your endpoints be accessed via private IPs and do you require DNS resolution outside our VPC?
03:52 Priya Nair: if you use VPC peering, you can hit our private IPs. with PrivateLink you get interface endpoints in your VPC which resolve to private ENIs, no public DNS needed. we will provide exact endpoints and IP ranges for firewall rules.
04:10 Carlos Ruiz: any concerns about cross-account ENI costs or limits? we have strict account-level quotas.
04:18 Marco Diaz: we'll coordinate with your SRE on quotas; PrivateLink consumes ENIs in subnets so subnet capacity matters. peering avoids ENIs but requires route table maintenance. we can provide a mini-test that uses a single AZ to reduce initial complexity.
04:36 Jordan Lee: shifting to benchmarks — Priya, can you walk through the plan?
04:41 Priya Nair: sure. Plan: Week 0 (this week) align on topology and sample prompts; Week 1 run network connectivity test + baseline latency (p50/p95) for short prompts and medium prompts; Week 2 run scale test to target 50 QPS and regression tests. metrics: p50, p95 latency, tokens/sec, error rate, throughput, and cost-per-1k tokens estimate. we'll produce a benchmark spreadsheet with raw samples.
05:08 Lena Park: for regression tests, we need to validate that model outputs don't degrade — is there a way to run evals against your gold prompts?
05:16 Priya Nair: yes we can run evals against your prompt set and produce delta metrics; we also support model pinning so the model version won't change during the POC.
05:24 Omar Ahmed: timeline constraints — we need a decision by mid-December. can the POC wrap within two weeks?
05:32 Jordan Lee: yes our standard POC is 2 weeks; if we start next week, we can aim to deliver results and a recommendation by 2026-12-10.
05:40 Dr. Maya Singh: what about data residency proofs — like a signed attestation or logs showing inter-region flows?
05:47 Marco Diaz: we can share flow logs and audit logs for the POC; we can also provide a short runbook showing how traffic stays in the region and that keys are customer-managed.
05:58 Carlos Ruiz: tokenization — our requests often include patient notes ~1,500 tokens for summaries; can the runtime handle longer seqs and do you recommend any quantization?
06:10 Priya Nair: yes longer sequences are supported. for throughput we need to size GPU/instance types. for POC we'll simulate longer sequences but the initial pilot you described (150 tokens avg) is light. if you need consistent long context we might recommend a model variant or kernel selection that handles 1k-2k tokens efficiently, or use KV cache strategies.
06:36 Lena Park: encryption concerns: do you support HSM or BYOK?
06:42 Marco Diaz: we support KMS integrations and customer-managed keys; HSM for private deployments is an option with extra configuration and a support contract.
06:52 Jordan Lee: anything else on networking?
06:55 Carlos Ruiz: about egress for telemetry — we want to ensure logs and metrics ship to our Prometheus/Grafana stack. can we push metrics over private links or via a collector in our VPC?
07:08 Priya Nair: yes metrics exporters can be placed in your VPC; we can also stream sanitized logs to a customer S3 bucket in your account over private routes.
07:18 Dr. Maya Singh: ok, let's capture the exact success criteria now so legal and infra are happy.
07:22 Jordan Lee: reiterating: 1) private connectivity (no public egress), 2) p95 latency <= 350ms for short prompts at pilot load, 3) support 50 QPS with <1% error, 4) audit logs and KMS BYOK, 5) data stored only in US region and evidence via logs. any additions?
07:45 Lena Park: add that access must be via SAML SSO and RBAC for role separation.
07:50 Jordan Lee: added.
07:52 Omar Ahmed: for sizing: we're expecting 10 concurrent active users, average 3 requests per user per minute during normal hours, peak 50 qps for batch processing. does Redwood have a cost estimate for that pilot?
08:05 Marco Diaz: we'll produce a rough cost estimate based on tokens/sec and instance hours for the POC; we'll include cost-of-serving and estimated per-1k token.
08:13 Priya Nair: for the benchmark assets we need from you: representative prompt set (CSV), sample payload sizes, CIDR ranges, and a staging AWS account or a test connectivity host accessible for the SEs.
08:26 Carlos Ruiz: we can provide a staging VPC and an SRE contact — that's in the action items.
08:32 Jordan Lee: perfect. I'll send the security pack (SOC2, ISO summary), and our Private deployment network checklist after the call.
08:38 Dr. Maya Singh: question about fallbacks — if private capacity isn't available, can requests fail open to hosted endpoints? we have to avoid that for PHI.
08:48 Marco Diaz: we can configure failover policies; for PHI you can disallow any fallback to hosted public endpoints. Redwood's routing supports canary and fallback but it's configurable per-customer.
08:59 Lena Park: great.
09:02 Jordan Lee: ok to recap next steps: we'll share network diagrams, security docs, and the benchmark plan. Kepler will share CIDRs, SRE contact, and prompt set. SEs will run tests and share results. schedule a results review on 2026-12-10.
09:19 Dr. Maya Singh: sounds good. thanks everyone.
09:23 Jordan Lee: thanks all — we'll follow up with the packets and calendar invite.
